verification_methodology_note: PRIMARY SOURCE ACCESS: laws.boe.gov.sa's LIVE portal was unreachable this pass (direct HTTPS and HTTP curl attempts to the exact law-detail URL [https://laws.boe.gov.sa/BoeLaws/Laws/LawDetails/9b61c9c0-71e2-4096-a3da-a9a700f2d79a/1] both returned curl exit code 28 / connection timeout, repeated). HOWEVER, a Wayback Machine snapshot of this exact BOE law page (archive.org/wayback/available confirmed a snapshot timestamped 20251212220818, the closest available when queried this pass) WAS reachable -- for THIS law the https:// scheme succeeded directly (HTTP 200, ~76KB) while the plain http:// scheme returned HTTP 403 for the same snapshot; both schemes were tried per this corpus's established practice and whichever worked was used, with no hostname tricks or bypass beyond the two established proxies (Wayback Machine / r.jina.ai). The archived page was parsed with BeautifulSoup (not naive regex/tag-stripping), locating each 'article_item' div and its 'HTMLContainer' child, recovering the complete text of all 28 articles, the decree number/date (مرسوم ملكي رقم م / 48 بتاريخ 13 / 8 / 1433, published 13/10/1433H), and BOE's own per-article HTML class attributes -- all 28 'article_item' divs carry ONLY the class 'no_alternate' (BOE's no-op/default marker), with zero occurrences of any amended/repealed marker class anywhere on the page. This is corroborated by BOE's page-level 'الحالة' (status) field reading 'ساري' (in force). SECONDARY CROSS-VERIFICATION: nezams.com (fetched live, directly, with a standard browser User-Agent header) provided an independent HTML transcription of all 28 articles under identical Arabic ordinal article headers (المادة الأولى .. المادة الثامنة والعشرون). A full text comparison of all 28 articles between the BOE-via-Wayback text and the nezams.com text found substantive agreement on all 28 articles with ZERO material differences (the only variation observed was nezams.com's use of an en-dash '–' where BOE uses a hyphen '-' in enumerated sub-item markers such as '2 - ' vs '2 – ', a cosmetic transcription-style artifact with no effect on legal meaning; this track's adopted text follows BOE's punctuation verbatim). nezams.com's own dedicated 'التعديلات' (amendments) metadata field independently states 'لم يجرى عليه تعديل' (no amendment has been made to it), matching BOE's lack of any per-article amendment marker. THIRD INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION: rulebook.sama.gov.sa (Saudi Central Bank's own official Rulebook portal -- a primary regulator-hosted source, since SAMA administers this Law per its own Article 27/28) hosts BOTH an official Arabic PDF (rulebook.sama.gov.sa/sites/default/files/ar_net_file_store/SAMA_AR_1073_VER1.pdf) and an official English-translation PDF (rulebook.sama.gov.sa/sites/default/files/en_net_file_store/SAMA_EN_1073_VER1.pdf) of this exact Law, each explicitly labeled with the same decree number/date. Both PDFs were downloaded directly and read in full (8 pages each); their article text agrees in substance with the BOE/nezams Arabic text for all 28 articles, and -- critically -- BOTH PDFs are the ONLY source in this pass that render the Law's chapter/فصل headings INLINE with the article text (neither BOE's nor nezams.com's per-article HTML view renders any فصل heading element inline; BOE's page only carries an unstructured prose 'نبذة عن النظام' summary describing five topical groups without stating exact article-number boundaries). The SAMA PDFs establish, with unambiguous heading placement, a 5-part structure: 'فصل تمهيدي / Introductory Chapter -- تعريفات / Definitions' (Article 1 only); 'الفصل الأول / Chapter One -- عقد الإيجار التمويلي / Finance Lease Contract' (Articles 2-17); 'الفصل الثاني / Chapter Two -- سجل العقود / Contract Register' (Articles 18-23); 'الفصل الثالث / Chapter Three -- المخالفات والمنازعات / Violations and Disputes' (Articles 24-26); 'الفصل الرابع / Chapter Four -- أحكام ختامية / Concluding Provisions' (Articles 27-28). See known_unresolved_discrepancies for a documented correction of an initial webpage-summary artifact regarding Chapter Two's exact span. No فرع (section) subdivisions exist anywhere in this Law (unlike some other tracks in this corpus) -- confirmed by the total absence of any 'الفرع' string in the BOE, nezams.com, or SAMA PDF texts. AMENDMENT STATUS: this Royal Decree (M/48, 13/8/1433H) itself has NEVER been amended since enactment, per BOE (zero per-article amendment markers), nezams.com (explicit 'لم يجرى عليه تعديل' statement), and a targeted web search for any amending Royal Decree (none found) alike -- all 28 articles are recorded as اصلية (original). The companion Implementing Regulation HAS itself been separately amended at least once (SAMA Rulebook: 'Amendment of Some Articles in the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Lease Law', amending inter alia Article 15 of the Regulation per Governor's Decision No. 93/م ش ت dated 18/10/1441H) -- see known_unresolved_discrepancies; this does NOT amend the primary Law's own text and is noted only for transparency, consistent with this pass ingesting the primary Law only. SUPERSESSION: no repeal/supersession clause naming a specific predecessor Finance Lease statute was found anywhere in the Law's 28 articles or its Royal Decree/Council of Ministers Resolution preamble -- see known_unresolved_discrepancies for the scope of this negative finding. COMPANION IMPLEMENTING REGULATION: confirmed to exist -- issued pursuant to Article 27 of this Law (الفصل الرابع: أحكام ختامية) by an Administrative/Governor's Decision numbered 1/م ش ت dated 14/4/1434H (per nezams.com's 'الملحقات' field), hosted on rulebook.sama.gov.sa and bfc.gov.sa. Consistent with this corpus's established precedent (banking_control_law, insurance_control_law, finance_companies_law, cooperative_health_insurance_law, healthcare_professions_law), this track ingests ONLY the primary 28-article Law; the Implementing Regulation is flagged as a follow-up candidate, not fabricated or partially guessed at. No legal text is altered. Arabic governs; no translation/paraphrase/interpretation performed on the Arabic text (the SAMA English PDF was used only for structural/chapter-title cross-checking, never as a source of Arabic wording). Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: An initial automated-summary rendering of rulebook.sama.gov.sa's Finance Lease Law webpage (obtained via a generic HTML-to-text fetch/summarization tool, before this track downloaded and read SAMA's own underlying PDF files directly) mis-stated Chapter Two's ('Contract Register') span as 'Articles 18-20' and Chapter Three's ('Violations and Disputes') span as 'Articles 24-26', leaving Articles 21-23 unassigned to any chapter in that summary. This was a webpage-summarization artifact, not a discrepancy in the primary legal text: this track subsequently downloaded SAMA's own official Arabic PDF (SAMA_AR_1073_VER1.pdf) and official English-translation PDF (SAMA_EN_1073_VER1.pdf) directly from rulebook.sama.gov.sa's file store and read them page-by-page in full. Both PDFs unambiguously place the 'Chapter Two / الفصل الثاني' heading immediately before Article 18, with NO further heading until 'Chapter Three / الفصل الثالث' appears immediately before Article 24 -- meaning Chapter Two / سجل العقود in the actual primary text spans Articles 18-23 (inclusive), not 18-20. This track's chapter_structure field reflects the verified 18-23 span read directly from the primary-source PDFs, not the erroneous initial webpage summary.

SAMA's own official English-translation PDF of this Law carries a footnote against Article 1's definition of 'SAMA' stating that the Saudi Arabian Monetary Agency was renamed 'Saudi Central Bank' pursuant to the Saudi Central Bank Law No. (M/36), dated 11/4/1442H corresponding to 26/11/2020G. This is an external renaming effected by a SEPARATE law (M/36), not a textual amendment to THIS Law: the Arabic text of this Law's own Article 1 (as confirmed identically by BOE-via-Wayback and by nezams.com, both fetched this pass) still reads 'المؤسسة: مؤسسة النقد العربي السعودي' and 'المحافظ: محافظ مؤسسة النقد العربي السعودي' verbatim, unchanged since 1433H. This track preserves the original 1433H Arabic defined terms exactly as published, consistent with the zero-fabrication/no-alteration rule, and documents the SAMA rename here only as external context, not as an in-force textual amendment to any article of this Law (BOE and nezams.com both independently confirm zero amendments to this Law's own text).

No repeal/supersession clause naming a specific predecessor Finance Lease statute or SAMA circular was found anywhere in this Law's 28 articles, nor in its Royal Decree or Council of Ministers Resolution preamble text (both fetched and read in full this pass). This differs from some other tracks in this corpus (e.g., healthcare_professions_law's Article 42, which expressly names two repealed prior statutes) -- this Law simply establishes finance leasing regulation without citing a specific prior instrument as repealed. Only a targeted search (BOE preamble text, plus general web search for any repeal announcement) was performed, not an exhaustive historical-archive audit, consistent with this pass's policy of 1-2 verification attempts per secondary fact before flagging remaining uncertainty rather than over-investing further search effort. This is recorded as a documented negative finding, not an assumption of completeness.

The Law's companion Implementing Regulation (اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام الإيجار التمويلي) is confirmed to exist -- issued pursuant to Article 27 of this Law by an Administrative/Governor's Decision numbered 1/م ش ت dated 14/4/1434H (per nezams.com's 'الملحقات' field), and is hosted on rulebook.sama.gov.sa and bfc.gov.sa. The Regulation has ITSELF been separately amended at least once since its issuance (SAMA Rulebook page 'Amendment of Some Articles in the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Lease Law', amending inter alia Article 15 of the Regulation per Governor's Decision No. 93/م ش ت dated 18/10/1441H) -- an amendment to the Regulation, not to the primary Law ingested in this track. Consistent with this corpus's established precedent for banking_control_law, insurance_control_law, finance_companies_law, cooperative_health_insurance_law and healthcare_professions_law (each of which identified but did not ingest its companion Implementing Regulation in the same pass as the primary Law), this track ingests ONLY the primary 28-article Law. The Implementing Regulation -- including its own amendment history -- is documented here as a candidate for a dedicated follow-up ingestion pass, not fabricated or partially guessed at.

Articles 20 and 22 contain genuine in-word decorative tatweel (ـ, kashida) stretching characters inside several words -- e.g. Article 20's 'مـع مـراعـاة ... المـادة ... المستأجـر ... الأصـل ... المـؤجَّـر' and Article 22's 'أثـناء'. This was verified NOT to be a scraping/extraction artifact of this pass's own tooling: the identical tatweel characters, in the identical positions within the identical words, are present in BOTH BOE-via-Wayback-Machine's HTML (fetched and parsed with BeautifulSoup this pass) AND in nezams.com's independently live-fetched HTML transcription of the same two articles (also fetched this pass, from an entirely separate site with its own separate scraping pipeline). Since two independent sources agree byte-for-byte on this typesetting feature, it is treated as a genuine characteristic of how these two articles were originally typeset/justified in the source document (a common practice for short justified table cells in Arabic legal typesetting) rather than a transcription error, and is preserved verbatim in this track's text rather than silently stripped. The track's validator carries a narrow, explicitly-keyed allowance for exactly these two articles (finance_lease_art_020, finance_lease_art_022) so that its general in-word-tatweel check still catches any *other*, unverified occurrence elsewhere in this track.
